# Cyberspace
Every network with a powered router has a region of cyberspace: a pad for each machine on it, paths along its cables, and a gate from the router's pad onto the data bus that joins every network to the city backbone. Pull a machine off the network and its pad and paths are gone; plug it back in and it's where it was. Regions line the bus on either side, each as big as its network, and a network that outgrows its region moves to a bigger one further along, taking any runners in it with it.
## Jacking in - Hold a [bold]cyberdeck[/bold] and use it on a networked machine: an [bold]access point[/bold] in the wall, a computer, a router. Beside it, you plug in; up to 8 tiles away and in sight, the deck reaches it through the air. - Your mind goes into your [bold]virtual body[/bold] in cyberspace, on a short spur beside the machine's pad. It has your shape, drawn in a flickering shade of your own colour, and wears a runner's uniform, but it doesn't breathe, and it bleeds [bold]ghostlight[/bold]. Your real body stays where it is, and can't do anything until you come back. - Use the deck in your hand instead to raise a [bold]practice grid[/bold]: a network of your own, with a training server, that nobody else can reach.
## Your deck Your virtual body is a computer, your deck, with an address on the network you came in through ([mono]ip[/mono] shows it). Its disk keeps its files between runs. Open its terminal from the action bar. Type [mono]colour #4de6ff[/mono] in it to change the colour you show in; anyone at your deck's terminal can change it too. Another runner who breaches your deck's node opens its terminal, files and all. It comes with the same examples as a programmable computer.
## Programs in hand Type [mono]hold FILE[/mono] at your deck to put a program in your virtual hand. Use it in your hand to run it on your deck, or use it on ICE or another runner to run it at them. Drop it and it's gone, though the file stays on your deck. Only one held program runs at a time. - [mono]hold blade[/mono]: your deck's weapon. Each strike takes a quarter of a runner's or ICE's [bold]integrity[/bold] (an eighth of a runner's through a ward), every two-thirds of a second, within reach. A runner with none left is cut out of cyberspace, with dumpshock; ICE derezzes. Used in your hand, it goes for the nearest ICE. It doesn't move you, so walk into reach yourself. - [mono]hold ward[/mono]: halves the strikes on you for two seconds, and can go up again six seconds later. - Write your own with [mono]new NAME deck[/mono], and read blade's or ward's with [mono]new NAME blade[/mono]. [mono]man deck[/mono] lists what a deck's programs can do.
## ICE [bold]ICE[/bold] guards a network: a spinning shape walking its paths, run by a program on one of its computers. A security computer starts its ICE when it boots, and any computer can start more with [mono]run ice_basic &[/mono]. ICE keeps to its network's region unless it's engaging a runner, when it follows them anywhere and comes back once it gives up. It leaves alone any runner whose ID the computer running it passes. Its colour says what it's doing: - [color=#BF4DFF]violet[/color]: patrolling from node to node. Three seconds in its sight (9 tiles along a clear path) and it comes for you. - [color=#FFCC26]yellow[/color]: searching for you where it last saw you. - [color=#FF2633]red[/color]: engaging. It chases you anywhere, even out of its network, and strikes when you're within reach: a quarter of your integrity once a second (an eighth through a ward). At none left you're thrown out with dumpshock and your head burns. Break its sight for eight seconds and it goes back to searching. Strike it back with your blade: four strikes derez it, and its program halts until someone runs it again. Practice grid ICE hits as hard but throws you out without dumpshock or burns. Write your own ICE with [mono]new NAME ice[/mono], or start from [mono]new NAME ice_basic[/mono]; [mono]man ice[/mono] lists what ICE can do.
## Firewalls
A [bold]network firewall[/bold] is a switch that guards the machines behind it: put it between a router and the rest of a network. In cyberspace its pad is shut like a locked door to any runner whose ID its reader doesn't pass. Stand at it for three seconds to breach it, and it lets you through until you jack out, but breaching it sets off every ICE on the network: [mono]ice_basic[/mono] comes straight for the firewall, engaging. Patrolling ICE stays on its own side of a firewall; searching or engaging ICE walks through it.
## Pushing files [mono]push FILE[/mono] copies a file from your deck onto the computer whose node you stand at, once its lock lets you (it's nobody's, your ID opens it, or you've breached it). [mono]push ADDR FILE[/mono] copies it over the network to a computer your ID opens. It lands under its own name, out of any folder.
## Using machines Use a machine's node to open it, as if you stood at the machine itself: a computer's terminal, a vending machine's stock, an air alarm's settings. You wear a [bold]proxy ID[/bold] that opens whatever the ID your real body wears opens. A machine your ID doesn't open is locked: stand at its node for three seconds to [bold]breach[/bold] it, and it stays breached until you jack out. Walk away from the node and the machine closes.
## Jacking out Jack out from the action bar at any time, at no cost. You're thrown out with [bold]dumpshock[/bold], ten seconds before you can jack in again, if: - the deck leaves your hands; - the machine goes off the network, or you lose range of it (2.5 tiles when plugged in) or sight of it (8 tiles through the air); - the path dissolves under you; - your body goes down.
